title: Decide secure contexts of top-level about:blank documents by origin
body: A top-level about:blank Document has about:blank as its top-level creation URL, which "Is url potentially trustworthy?" always accepts. The secure context algorithm now uses the environment's top-level origin for these instead. This changes three cases: * A Document created by navigating a top-level traversable to about:blank was a secure context regardless of its origin. This meant an http: page could navigate a same-origin popup to about:blank and use [SecureContext] APIs through it. It is now a secure context only if its origin is potentially trustworthy, matching the behaviour of Chromium, Webkit, and Gecko. * #13103 made a popup's initial about:blank Document copy its creator's top-level creation URL. That is wrong when the creator is a non-secure context with a potentially trustworthy origin, such as an https: iframe in an http: page: the popup was not a secure context, and neither was the same-origin Document that later reused its Window. That step is reverted where instead the popup is now decided by its own origin, matching the behaviour of Chromium, Gecko and WebKit. * A popup's about:blank Document with an opaque origin, such as one opened by a sandboxed iframe with allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox, is not a secure context, since an opaque origin is never potentially trustworthy. This matches WebKit. Tests: https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/64008 Follow up to https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/13103, Fixes https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/13109 --- I am not 100% confident in these changes - though to my understanding they do seem very sensible and more correct - it took me a few attempts before I could get the test matrix matching. In particular, I am a little confused about the last bulleted above. I am not sure what behaviour should be specified here, WebKit one seems simplest to me, so I've gone with that. Firefox/Chromium might have better behaviour though. --- - [ ] At least two implementers are interested (and none opposed): * Webkit (implements, pending decision on last bullet) * … - [x] [Tests](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt) are written and can be reviewed and commented upon at: * https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/64008 - [ ] [Implementation bugs](https://github.com/whatwg/meta/blob/main/MAINTAINERS.md#handling-pull-requests) are filed: * Chromium: … * Gecko: … * WebKit: … * Deno (only for timers, structured clone, base64 utils, channel messaging, module resolution, web workers, and web storage): … * Node.js (only for timers, structured clone, base64 utils, channel messaging, and module resolution): … - [x] Corresponding [HTML AAM](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/) & [ARIA in HTML](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/) issues & PRs: N/A - [x] [MDN issue](https://github.com/whatwg/meta/blob/main/MAINTAINERS.md#handling-pull-requests) is filed: N/A - [x] The top of this comment includes a [clear commit message](https://github.com/whatwg/meta/blob/main/COMMITTING.md) to use.
